transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-24
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Amy Li (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Michael Park (NexaHealth Eng Mgr), Priya Rao (Infra), Samira Khan (Security), Jon Ortiz (Data Platform)

Summary: quick check on onboarding steps, we ran a first bench, some network access missing, security questions. agreed next steps and owners.

[00:00] Amy Li: hey everyone, thanks for joining, how's it going on your side?
[00:12] Michael Park: yeah hi Amy, hey Carlos, thanks. overall good, we're a little stuck on the VPC peering appendix, priya's been looking at that.
[00:20] Priya Rao: yep, we tried to follow the onboarding doc but the service account permission set didn't quite match our org policy, we need the exact scopes you need.
[00:32] Carlos Mendes: okay, cool, that's helpful. I can post the minimal IAM roles right after the call. it's basically: compute read, route tables read, and a managed service account for the connector. we mislabeled it in the doc as "redwood connector role" so maybe that caused confusion.
[00:48] Amy Li: and just to set expectations, for the smoke test we only need read access to the VPC metadata and an outbound route to your egress, we don't need full admin.
[01:05] Samira Khan: quick question on encryption - do you require bringing your own keys or can you manage keys? we prefer KMS managed by our security team, and if there's HSM needed we need that flagged.
[01:18] Carlos Mendes: great question. Redwood supports both KMS and external HSM via our private deployment path; for hosted/dedicated pilot you can use your cloud KMS, we store keys transiently and we have audit logs. i'll attach the SOC2 section again - sorry if earlier doc had a typo, it said "SOC II".
[01:33] Michael Park: ok. about the initial benchmark you ran last week - we saw the sheet, but can you walk through the tuning knob changes you made?
[01:40] Carlos Mendes: yes so in the first pass we ran two configs: default and caching enabled. default had token p50 around 310ms, caching reduced that to about 180ms for repeated prefixes. note the model variant was the 13B open-weights, we called it "redwood-13b-v1" in the sheet but the model registry shows variant names differently, so apologies for the naming slip.
[02:10] Priya Rao: when you say caching, is that prefix kv cache? will that store any customer data persistently?
[02:18] Carlos Mendes: it's KV prefix caching - by default it's ephemeral and tied to the session; in Dedicated you can enable disk-backed cache per customer but it's encrypted and we can configure TTLs. we can also disable it if policy forbids caching.
[02:33] Jon Ortiz: any chance to see the raw tokens/latency distribution? the sheet has averages only.
[02:40] Carlos Mendes: yes i'll export the per-request CSV and drop a link; i'll also include the prompt set we used.
[02:47] Amy Li: good. next, access status - priya, you mentioned the service account mismatch, anything else?
[02:55] Priya Rao: also need the CIDR ranges you expect to peer with and the ports to open, we saw a note that you need 443 outbound but want to confirm anything else.
[03:04] Carlos Mendes: just 443 outbound for the control plane; for dedicated/private there may be additional intra-node ports but those are only for private deployments. we'll put exact CIDR list in the checklist.
[03:18] Samira Khan: on logs and auditability - how long do you retain request logs and can we push them to our SIEM?
[03:25] Amy Li: we can stream audit logs to your SIEM and retention is configurable; default retention for pilot is 30 days but enterprises often request 90/365 - we'll include options.
[03:38] Michael Park: perfect. timeline: we're hoping to run smoke test by end of next week. is that reasonable?
[03:45] Amy Li: yes if we get the service account + VPC read by Tues we can kick off smoke tests Wed/Thu and share results by Friday. Carlos, is that timeline ok from SE side?
[03:55] Carlos Mendes: yep we can do a focused smoke run, will enable prefix caching and run the benchmark set; i'll also test with quantized model variant to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[04:07] Michael Park: good. one blocker i want to flag - procurement needs an SSO/SAML integration doc and show that single-tenant logs are supported for compliance.
[04:18] Samira Khan: and we need confirmation about data residency for the pilot - the data shouldn't leave our EU region.
[04:25] Carlos Mendes: for hosted we can route to region-specific endpoints and for Dedicated we can provision in-region capacity. i'll note that and include region config options.
[04:36] Amy Li: ok let's recap the owners and next steps..
[04:40] Amy Li: Redwood will send updated onboarding checklist, full IAM role list, CIDR ranges, SOC2 and KMS/HSM notes, and the benchmark csv + prompts.
[04:52] Michael Park: NexaHealth to provide service account, network CIDRs, and schedule infra deep-dive with Priya and Jon.
[05:01] Samira Khan: i'll send over the security questionnaire answers and indicate if HSM is required.
[05:09] Amy Li: sounds good - we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive and the smoke test window.
[05:16] Carlos Mendes: one small note - when you run the second benchmark we recommend toggling quantization to see cost delta; i'll include the script.
[05:25] Michael Park: great. thanks everyone.
[05:30] Amy Li: thanks, talk soon.

Links & references mentioned: pilot checklist: https://redwood.ai/docs/pilot-checklist ; benchmark sheet (will be shared): https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/nexa-pilot (placeholder)

End of transcript.
